header: Which questions belong to EXECUTIVE DEEP SYNTHESIS (EDS)? I made this a pure, explainable detector so the one Enter key can decide instead of a button. It reads the question only (no database, no model) and returns a score, a level and the reasons. THE PATTERN (found in the questions I marked as EDS: the four tests of the old query document and the "C" questions of the accuracy test, and checked against the Smart Semantic questions of the same document and the 210 other acceptance questions): A Smart Semantic question asks ONE thing that ONE circular answers ("How do I return my provident fund advance...?"). An EDS question needs the answer to be BUILT from SEVERAL documents, versions or periods. It shows in four ways:
1. an ANALYTIC TASK VERB: trace / evolution, contrast, compare, synthesize, cross-reference, briefing, summarize ... (all four old tests start with one; none of the 215 other questions contains one);

2. a VERSION RELATION between documents: "change(d) between", "what changed", "original ... corrected", "first announced", "earlier circular" (three of the four "C" questions; none of the 215 others);
3. an AGGREGATE across a period: "list the ... events ... in December 2024";

4. DISCOVERY / DATA-MINING language, the kind a policy maker uses to see what is normally invisible: correlate, hidden, overlooked, "what are we missing", inconsistencies, gaps, contradictions, implications, insights (decisive); patterns, trends, themes, what emerges or is revealed, relationships and connections between things, overlap, divergence, impact of X on Y, "how often", "across all circulars / years / schemes" (supporting, they need one more cue);

5. supporting shape: TWO OR MORE YEARS named ("from 2023 to 2024", "the 2024 and 2025 schemes"), a second verb, TWO questions joined by "and which / and what", MANY NAMED things (6 to 11 capitalised names in the old tests), and LENGTH (29 to 44 words in the old tests; the longest ordinary question has 19).

"Data mining" here means: find what is hidden in the circulars by relating facts that look unrelated (a safety rule and an electoral-roll declaration; welfare schemes and attendance systems; how often a decision is revised after it is announced). Each feature has a weight. 5 or more = EDS ("synthesis"), 3 or 4 = "borderline" (a written summary may help: e.g. "Summarise the Mediclaim extension circular"), below 3 = an ordinary question. Supporting shape alone can never reach 5: a question must also have a verb, a version relation or an aggregate, or several supporting features at once. GUARD: a question about PEOPLE DATA (who is the head / senior / designation / ticket / mobile ...) is never EDS, even if it says "compare": "compare the seniority of X and Y" belongs to the employee directory. (The old tests say "employees" and "executives" only as the groups a policy applies to, so I do not let those words block.) This detects the INTENT only. Whether synthesis then runs also needs a logged-in executive (the screen) that the server verifies again, and the switch (ON by default since step 41a; NEXT_PUBLIC_FRONT_PATH_AUTO_EDS=false turns it off). I never decide those here. If an automatic synthesis finds no relevant circular, the screen falls back to the normal search (useOmniSearch.ts).

members.name: reasons
doc: What fired, in plain words (shown in tests, the trace and the report).

members.name: blockedBy
doc: Set when the question looks like a people-data question, which is never EDS.

symbols.name: DISCOVERY_STRONG
symbols.sig: const DISCOVERY_STRONG = /\b(correlat\w+|hidden|unforeseen|overlooked|unnoticed|invisible|blind spots?|what are we missing|anomal\w+|inconsisten\ …
doc: DISCOVERY, decisive (+5): words that name an act of finding what is hidden or relating the unrelated. They are rare in ordinary lookups.

symbols.name: DISCOVERY_MEDIUM
doc: DISCOVERY, supporting (+2 for EACH distinct cue, up to three): common words that signal pattern-finding. One alone never reaches EDS; several together ("recurring themes", "trend" + "how many circulars were issued ... each of the last three years") do.

symbols.name: TWO_TOPICS
doc: TWO TOPICS asked of the circulars in one breath ("what do the circulars say about X and about Y"): the answer is built from the circulars of both topics. A Gaurav Diwas circular and a Flag Day circular (11 Nov 2026) scored 2 and took the plain path, which is why I added this.

symbols.name: ASKS_AFTER_COLON
doc: THREE OR MORE ASKS listed after a colon ("dates, how employees take part, and the ways to pay"): I want a briefing with a part for each, not one passage

symbols.name: BREAKDOWN
doc: A STAGE-BY-STAGE or CATEGORY-BY-CATEGORY breakdown ("what follows each violation at each stage", "for every level", "grade-wise"): the answer is a table of several rows, not one passage.

symbols.name: PEOPLE_OPS
doc: People-data operations: the employee directory answers these, never a synthesis of circulars. My guard looks for the DIRECTORY sense of a word, not the bare word: "who" / "whom" / "grade" / "junior" are everyday words of policy questions ("those who do not register", "through whom is it issued", "by grade", "Junior Officers of the 2008 batch"), and blocking on them kept strong EDS questions (a compare, a stage-by-stage ladder) out of EDS. What stays blocking: whose <person field>, "who is the head / manager / in-charge ...", "who has / have / got ..." (a roster; not "who has to submit"), senior / junior used for a person (not "Senior Officers", "Junior Officers"), seniority, designation, ticket, mobile / phone, e-mail, surname, headcount.

symbols.name: namedThings
doc: I count distinct capitalised words, acronyms and #numbers that are not the first word: this is the "many named things" signal.

symbols.name: autoEdsEnabled
symbols.sig: export function autoEdsEnabled(env: Record<string, string | undefined> = { NEXT_PUBLIC_FRONT_PATH_AUTO_EDS: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FRONT_PATH_AUTO_EDS }): boolean
doc: ON by default (step 41a): the Enter key sends an EDS-type question from a logged-in executive to Executive Deep Synthesis by itself (the screen decides, OmnibarModal.tsx; the server still verifies the executive from the login session). I removed the button, so there is none any more. The kill switch is NEXT_PUBLIC_FRONT_PATH_AUTO_EDS=false (also 0, off, no, in any case). It is a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable because the browser reads it, so a change needs a new deployment. The browser must pass the value in explicitly, because Next only replaces the literal process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_... in client code.
